title: This Desert Bird Carries Water to Its Chicks in Its Feathers

scenes.text: This bird carries drinking water to its chicks, and it doesn't use its beak.
Sandgrouse live in deserts, and their chicks hatch many miles from the nearest water.
So the father flies over twenty kilometers to a waterhole and soaks his belly in it.
His belly feathers have tiny coiled barbs that soak up about twenty-five milliliters of water.
During the half-hour flight home, about half of it evaporates. The chicks drink the rest straight from his feathers.
A bird that works as a flying water bottle.

description:
A male sandgrouse soaks his belly feathers at a waterhole and flies over twenty kilometers to bring water to his chicks.
His feathers hold about twenty-five milliliters, and the chicks drink it straight from them.
Would you have guessed a feather could do that?
